scenes.caption: Record a person's key once you have it from them directly. The CRM then shows who has a verified key.

card.title: Verified keys on people
card.sub: Record a person's key once you have it from them directly. Then the CRM shows who has a verified key.
card.foot: Two made-up people: you are Sam Sample, and Rui Kowalski is a demo contact. Keys and fingerprints are hidden.

scenes.caption: First, log in: the key is signed for with your own browser key. Here you are Sam Sample.
On a company's page, each person shows No key yet, or their verified key. Rui Kowalski has none.
Add their key: drop the QR code Rui sent you from their You page, or paste its text. Only add a key you got from them directly.
Here, Rui's key text, pasted and hidden, and how it reached you: their key text.
The page checks it and shows what will be written: Rui's key and its fingerprint, signed for by you. The file's contents are hidden here.
Write it, and Rui shows Verified key, with the start of its fingerprint.
Contacts has a Key column: who has a verified key, and who has none yet.
A key you verified yourself is how you know who you are sending to, without trusting anyone in between.

card.title: Why it matters
card.sub: A key you verified yourself is how you know who you are sending to, without trusting anyone in between.
